pages.text: Two **Wheels**, a row of planks for the bed, and two slabs on top. Make the wheels first.

pages.title: Hitch and Haul
pages.text:
Slot the cart into the **Upgraded Saddle** and it appears behind your horse, rolling along as you ride. It shares the stabilizer's slot, so a horse carries one or the other - not both.

Quickest way to fit one: right-click the horse holding the cart. It goes straight on, as long as the horse wears an Upgraded Saddle and that slot is empty.

pages.title: Park It Anywhere
pages.text:
Right-click the ground with the cart to stand one up on its own, shafts down, no horse needed. A parked cart is decoration - nobody rides it - but a **Chest** works on it exactly as it does on a hitched one.

Hit it a few times to pick it back up, like a boat. Break one with a chest fitted and the chest and everything in it come down with it.

pages.title: Room for Four
pages.text:
An empty cart seats four. Two share the driver's bench up front - whoever takes it first drives the horse - and two more ride in the bed behind.

Animals that wander into the bed climb aboard on their own, and once you're driving, one can ride shotgun in the free seat beside you. The cart takes anything a **boat** would.

**Sneak** and right-click an animal to set it down, or the cart itself to unload the lot.

pages.title: Fitting a Chest
pages.text:
Right-click the cart with a **Chest** in hand to mount it in the bed. **Sneak** and right-click the cart to open it - a full **double chest** of room, and the lid swings up while you're browsing.

The chest fills the bed, so a cart hauling cargo carries no back-seat passengers - the driver's bench still seats two.

pages.title: Taking It Off
pages.text:
**Shears** take the chest back off and drop it beside the horse. Empty it first - a loaded chest refuses to come off rather than spill across the road.

Things come off in the order they went on, and the slot flashes **red** if you try to skip a step: shear the chest off before unhitching the cart, and unhitch the cart before taking the saddle off.
